Cyber Attack Disrupts Indonesian Engineering Firms, Operations Restored After Ransomware Incident

JAKARTA, June 14 — Several major engineering and construction firms across Indonesia resumed operations this week after a ransomware attack crippled key IT systems and project management platforms, industry sources said Thursday.

The incident, which began late last week, targeted the core digital infrastructure of at least four prominent companies, including Nusantara BuildTech and Garuda Engineering Solutions, according to the Indonesian Engineering & Construction Association (IECA). The cyber attack encrypted confidential design files, financial records, and communications, halting work at multiple sites and delaying project deliveries.

"This was the most significant cyber incident our sector has faced in recent years," IECA Chairperson Rizky Pranata told reporters. "Critical data was inaccessible for several days, and ongoing construction projects in Jakarta, Surabaya, and Bali were affected."

Sources familiar with the investigation said the attackers demanded a ransom in cryptocurrency in exchange for decryption keys. The affected firms, working closely with Indonesia’s National Cyber and Crypto Agency (BSSN) and external cybersecurity consultants, ultimately regained access to their data without paying the ransom. Officials declined to specify the technical measures used, citing ongoing investigations.

By Tuesday evening, most affected companies had restored their systems from secure backups and resumed project work. "We have been able to bring our operations back online and are implementing additional security protocols to prevent future incidents," said a spokesperson for Nusantara BuildTech.

Industry analysts estimate the disruption caused direct losses of at least IDR 45 billion (about USD 2.8 million), largely from project delays and additional IT recovery costs. "This event highlights how vital robust cybersecurity is for engineering firms, especially as they rely increasingly on digital tools for design, procurement, and project coordination," said Dimas Hartono, a Jakarta-based cybersecurity analyst.

The IECA has urged members to conduct urgent reviews of their cybersecurity infrastructure and to increase staff training on phishing and other common attack vectors. The union representing engineering workers, Serikat Pekerja Teknik Indonesia, welcomed the swift resumption of operations but called for long-term investments to protect jobs and data.

"We are relieved the situation was resolved without major layoffs," said union leader Lestari Widodo. "But the sector must treat cyber threats as a permanent risk."

Authorities said the investigation into the perpetrators continues.
